column1: # tests/memfn/simd_accept.tsv -- THE SIMD ACCEPTANCE RECORD ([MEMFN] R4e'
# batch 1, R-13; docs/design/memfn/integration.md §R4.9.6 "The acceptance
# record and its lifecycle"). One line per SIMD row x level x official CPU
# class (§R4.9.5's table: w16 and w32 are judged on ubuntubudu, Zen 1, AND
# the dev box, Zen 4). A row lands ONLY with a CANDIDATE line per level and
# class (rows_check.py check F, `make test-memfn-rows`).
# state  CANDIDATE (landed behind -fmemfn-simd, OFF by default, tier-U
#        evidence only), ACCEPTED (a tier-O bench reading met the bar on every
#        official box running the level), STALE (the comparator moved; reads
#        as CANDIDATE until re-measured), REJECTED (a tier-O loss).
# tier   unofficial | bench. Only a `bench` line may be ACCEPTED or REJECTED.
# The digests and the transcript are written by a TIMING RUN, never by hand:
# C19 (the comparator/transcript digest check) is born with the first
# transcript; until then every line is CANDIDATE with `-` in those columns
# and check F says the C19 half is UNREACHED.
# row
vrun-w16
vrun-w16
vrun-w32
